clue.text: Taking a rest, crews may get a salad

indicators.note: the letters of the words a rest and crews may get rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A rowing crew, pausing for a break, might tuck into a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may get' is the anagram signal: the ten letters of A REST and CREWS are rearranged. 'Taking' only links the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This peppery leaf, grown in running water, is a classic salad green.

clue.text: Decline a new fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters of a new are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a trendy new style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun but works as a verb, the anagram signal for A NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to dwindle or diminish, as the moon does after it is full.

clue.text: A loud-mouthed individual proclaiming his intelligence

definitions.text: A loud-mouthed individual proclaiming his intelligence

parts.words: A loud-mouthed individual proclaiming his intelligence
parts.note: intelligence here means news, not brainpower: the man is a traditional public announcer shouting out the latest notices in the street

explanation.surface: A braggart loudly shows off how clever he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' reads as cleverness, but means news; the loud-mouthed individual is the old-style public announcer of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: In earlier times this official walked the streets ringing a bell and shouting public announcements.

clue.text: A poor player cut short the minister

indicators.note: the word for the poor player is clipped, losing its final letter

parts.note: in cricket and golf slang a rabbit is a weak, unskilled player

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is hopeless at games has his innings ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last letter, T, from RABBIT. A rabbit is British sports slang for a feeble player, especially a tail-end batsman in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher and leader of a congregation is its minister.

clue.text: Patches a salesman displays

parts.note: rep is short for representative, a travelling salesman
to air something is to display or show it off

explanation.surface: A salesman shows off his range of patches.
explanation.definitionFit: Patches are mends made to damaged things, so they are fixes or mendings.

clue.text: A quarter request the queen to get a rose

parts.note: S, for south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
to pray is to ask earnestly, to request
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Someone asks the queen for a quarter of her garden so they can grow a rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rose' is not the flower but the perforated nozzle on a watering can or hose.
explanation.definitionFit: The rose of a watering can is its perforated spout, a device that scatters water in droplets.

clue.text: Merry monarch being firm with the French

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A jolly king does business with France.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme's Old King Cole was 'a merry old soul'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme king is famed for being a merry old soul calling for his pipe and bowl.

clue.text: A diamond ring must be given up, that's the conclusion

indicators.note: in a down clue given up means the pieces are written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a diamond is a precious stone, a gem
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone has to hand back a diamond engagement ring, and that is the end of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be given up' turns A, GEM and O round in this down clue, making the reading OMEGA from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Real men, yet can be easily understood

indicators.note: the letters of real men yet can be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Real men, it turns out, are not so hard to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is the anagram signal for the ten letters of REAL MEN and YET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic and simple, as in Holmes's supposed line about deduction, is readily grasped.

clue.text: Lively exchange concerning some key point

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
part means some of something
E is a musical key
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A heated discussion about a crucial point in the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key point' looks like one idea but gives two letters: E as a musical key and E as a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick witty retorts traded back and forth make up a lively conversation.

clue.text: Mohammedan prince turning a degree pale

indicators.note: the pieces for the degree and for pale are turned round and read from right to left

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree
wan means pale and sickly

explanation.surface: A Muslim prince grows pale on receiving a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses BA + WAN as a whole, giving NAW + AB.
explanation.definitionFit: A nawab was a Muslim ruler or governor in Mughal India, a princely title.

clue.text: Stick with bluish grey coating always

indicators.note: the colour word coats or wraps around the word for always

parts.note: perse is an old word for a dark bluish-grey colour
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on applying a bluish-grey paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick with' is the definition, a verb phrase meaning keep at it. Perse is a rare old colour word, worth knowing for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is to stick with a task until it is done.

clue.text: It's clear in a built-up area there's a certain harshness

indicators.note: the word for clear is placed inside the word for the built-up area

parts.note: a city is a large built-up area
to rid a place of something is to clear it

explanation.surface: Clearly, a built-up area has a certain harshness about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'there's a certain' are only links. 'clear' is a verb here, meaning remove or get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: Acridity is pungency or bitterness, and so a sharp, harsh quality of taste, smell or temper.

clue.text: Conscious of a sign of nautical progress

parts.note: the wake is the trail of disturbed water left behind a moving ship

explanation.surface: Someone is aware of a ship's progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conscious means being alert and not asleep.

clue.text: Diversions causing controversy?

parts.note: the pastimes are puzzles, and read as two words they are angry words that cause arguments

explanation.surface: Pastimes that stir up argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the answer becomes cross words, an angry exchange; whole, it is a puzzle like this one.
explanation.definitionFit: These puzzles are a popular diversion, and as two words they mean an argument.

clue.text: Commuters complaining bitterly?

parts.note: read one way it describes those who travel by train; read another it describes people who rail, that is protest bitterly

explanation.surface: Commuters grumble angrily about their journey.
explanation.walkthrough: To rail against something is to complain bitterly; the clue imagines the term also meaning people who go by train.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rail are scolders and complainers, and the word playfully suggests train travellers too.

clue.text: Charm one's way in

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to charm someone is to delight or enchant them
the door or opening by which someone goes in

explanation.surface: A charmer finds their route into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Stressed on the second syllable it means to enchant; on the first, a doorway or point of access.

clue.text: Pull in military men and plot

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a tract is a stretch or plot of land

explanation.surface: Soldiers and a conspiracy are hauled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme but means a piece of land, a tract.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract is to draw back in, as a cat does its claws.

clue.text: Fixing up a telephone, phoned in

indicators.note: the word for phoned goes inside the word for telephone

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them
rang is the past tense of ring, meaning phoned

explanation.surface: Someone sorts things out by making a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixing up' is the definition, meaning organising, not mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging something means organising or setting it up.

clue.text: Exaggerate the time spent in prison

definitions.meaning: to overstate, as in pulling a fact out of shape
a period of imprisonment, a term inside

explanation.surface: An inmate overstates how long his sentence is.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull the truth too far is to overstate it, and slang also uses the word for a jail term.

clue.text: The woman holding a contest for the not-so-slim

indicators.note: the word for the woman holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: her is a word for the woman
to vie is to compete, to contest

explanation.surface: A woman enters a competition for larger people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the not-so-slim' is a playful definition: a comparative adjective standing for plumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Being not so slim means weighing more, being comparatively plump.

clue.text: He gets wool from the sheep he rears possibly

definitions.text: He gets wool from the sheep

indicators.note: possibly shows that the letters of he rears may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A farmer who raises sheep also clips their fleeces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' is the anagram signal for HE REARS.
explanation.definitionFit: This farm worker clips the fleece off the animals.

clue.text: Shrub bearing white flowers used in posy-ring arrangements

indicators.note: the answer is spelt out inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A white-flowered shrub goes into posies and ring-shaped flower displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' signals that the answer runs through po(SY-RING A)rrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the mock orange or lilac, a bush with fragrant white blossom.

clue.text: Centre-forward accompanied by a woman

indicators.note: the centre of the word forward is its middle letter

parts.note: and joins one thing with another, as if accompanied by it

explanation.surface: A football striker goes out with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre-forward' looks like the football position, but gives the central letter of 'forward', W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanda is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Sound distortion is the difficulty

indicators.note: distortion twists the letters of the word sound out of shape

explanation.surface: A fuzzy audio signal is the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distortion' is the anagram signal for SOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodus is a knotty point or complication, a problem to be untangled.

clue.text: Distress occasioned about border plant

indicators.note: the word for distress goes around the word for border

parts.note: agony is extreme distress
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A gardener is upset by something in the flower border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasioned' is only a link. 'border' suggests a flower bed, fitting the plant, but gives an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family.

clue.text: Well-qualified persons — really tip-top people

parts.note: MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree
A1 means first-rate, read here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Highly qualified graduates are truly first-class people.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means excellent; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Grasping what is suggested by "average"

definitions.meaning: the arithmetical middle value of a set of numbers

explanation.surface: A miser is what the word average brings to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-fisted person is stingy, and in statistics the word names the central value.

clue.text: Courted in order to obtain discount

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters of courted in are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone woos a seller to get money off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' belongs to the fodder; 'order' is the anagram signal for COURTED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount is a cut in price.

clue.text: The team accepting money may well go downhill fast!

indicators.note: the word for the team takes in the letter for money

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A team that takes bribes is likely to decline rapidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts L inside SIDE. 'may well' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To slide is to glide quickly downwards, as on ice or a slope.

clue.text: Very big-hearted, but indifferent

indicators.note: the letters for big are put in the heart of the word for very

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
OS stands for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: Someone is generous, yet unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big-hearted' suggests generosity, but 'big' is OS (outsize) and 'hearted' puts it in the middle of the word for very.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only middling, neither good nor bad, is mediocre.

clue.text: Getting used to forcing an entry?

definitions.meaning: wearing new shoes until comfortable, or accustoming a horse to work
entering a building illegally by force

explanation.surface: A burglar is still adjusting to his trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing in new boots is one sense; a burglar's illegal entry into a house is the other.
